page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.8-128 is a flexible compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 16 virtual CPUs derived from 8 dedicated physical cores. The instance is powered by Intel Xeon 8358 processors running at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz, supporting two threads per core with dedicated allocation. The configuration provides 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 8.0 GB of memory allocated per execution thread.

The virtual machine does not include bundled local disk storage or hardware-based GPU accelerators. Persistent and boot disk operations rely entirely on attached network block volumes, and network ingress/egress is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because execution resources are backed by dedicated physical cores rather than shared or burstable capacity, CPU scheduling remains deterministic across varying thread counts.

With 128 GB of RAM allocated across 16 vCPUs, VM.Standard3.Flex.8-128 delivers strong memory density relative to core count, making it cost-efficient for workloads constrained by memory footprints rather than raw compute cycles. A primary operational consideration is the reliance on remote storage, which shifts I/O throughput dependencies onto block storage performance rather than local disk buses. The instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, including medium-scale relational databases, in-memory caching solutions, enterprise application runtimes, and analytics pipelines.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.8-128 is a memory-dense compute instance within the Standard family, configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores and 128.0 GB of system memory. Powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8358 processor running at 2.6 GHz with simultaneous multithreading, it delivers an expansive 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks integrated local disk storage and discrete GPUs, utilizing remote block volumes for persistent storage and supplying one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated allocation of compute cores eliminates hypervisor resource contention, providing consistent performance across system threads. This combination of high memory capacity and predictable compute makes the instance an effective choice for memory-intensive applications, in-memory caching services, mid-sized relational databases, and enterprise software stacks requiring substantial working memory per thread.
